Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing and limiting questions to one and a follow-up will be provided. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, our management team will cover key highlights in these areas: revenue performance by segment, aftermarket and services growth, drivers behind aftermarket strength, our R&D investments in next-generation platforms, and the key assumptions underlying our guidance.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our Glide Breaker hypersonic program and its potential to enhance strategic deterrence capabilities for our customers. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 sustainment and next-gen weapons, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with ramps on narrowbody and widebody deliveries.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan. Now, let's turn to the financials. In the third quarter, we reported revenue of $12.4 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.80, up from $2.40 in the prior year period. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $8.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at revenue of $68 to $72 billion, up 6% to 10% year-over-year at the midpoint, segment-adjusted operating margins expanding 50 to 100 basis points to 11.5% to 12.5%, free cash flow of $6.5 to $7.5 billion, and EPS of $28.50 to $30.00. These figures reflect our confidence in executing a $165 billion backlog—80% of which is funded—with a book-to-bill ratio holding steady at 1.2x.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 22.1%, up 120 basis points year-over-year; operating income of $2.1 billion, a 14% increase; and free cash flow of $1.5 billion for the quarter. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives, while focused on returning capital to shareholders through our quarterly dividend and ongoing share repurchases.

Diving deeper into our segment performance, consolidated revenues reached $12.4 billion, up 15% year-over-year, driven by strong execution across all segments amid a stabilizing supply chain and robust demand signals. Our book-to-bill ratio stands at 1.2x, with a record backlog of $185 billion providing exceptional visibility.

Commercial Aerospace, which accounted for 42% of total revenues, delivered $5.2 billion, a robust 28% increase year-over-year. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, fueled by the continued ramp-up on key narrowbody and widebody programs. Deliveries of our GAD-900 twin-aisle platform hit 18 units this quarter, up from 12 a year ago, as we resolve legacy supply chain bottlenecks in titanium forgings and composite structures from our European suppliers. OEM revenues grew 32%, propelled by surging orders from Asia-Pacific carriers, notably our partnership with a major Chinese lessor for 50 GAD-700 narrowbodies, contributing $1.1 billion in milestone payments as China's aviation market rebounds to 95% of pre-pandemic levels per IATA data. Engine aftermarket pull-through was strong, with GTF-powered units showing improved on-wing time thanks to digital twin analytics reducing unplanned shop visits by 22%. Headwinds included LEAP-1A engine delays shaving $150 million off the top line and Boeing 737 MAX pauses pressuring aerostructure content. Regionally, North America grew 35% on Delta and United ramp-ups, EMEA was flat at +2% due to Ryanair's cautious planning amid high fuel costs. Margins expanded 220 basis points to 14.2%, driven by fixed-price efficiencies and additive manufacturing scale-up at our Charleston facility. Looking ahead, we're leaning into sustainability like our SAF-blend certified GAD-X hybrid-electric demonstrator targeting 2026 certification for EU ReFuelEU mandates.

Shifting to Defense, our largest segment at 49% of revenues, we posted $6.1 billion, up 10% year-over-year—a solid performance in a budget-constrained environment. Growth was anchored by fixed-wing sustainment and next-gen weapons, with F-35 Lot 18-20 LRIP deliveries to Lockheed Martin contributing $2.3 billion, including advanced wingbox assemblies with integrated health monitoring via fiber optic sensors. Missile and precision munitions surged 18%, boosted by DoD replenishment post-Ukraine attrition on JASSM-ER and our hypersonic glide vehicle booster stage entering low-rate production ahead of schedule. Space revenues jumped 25% to $850 million, driven by NASA Artemis SLS solid rocket boosters and a $400 million award for hypersonic reentry vehicle payloads under SDA Tranche 2 Tracking Layer. U.S. revenues grew 12% on the FY2024 NDAA's $886 billion topline, international sales—35% of the segment—rose 5%, tempered by FMS delays in the Middle East amid tensions. Europe stood out at +15% with A400M wing upgrades and Polish PZL M28 sustainment. Challenges included labor shortages in Fort Worth, mitigated via India partnerships. Book-to-bill was 1.3x with $8.2 billion in new awards, including hypersonics IDIQ. Segment margins held at 12.8%, with upside from cost-plus on classified programs.

Services rounded out at 9% of revenues with $1.1 billion, up 18% year-over-year, outpacing OEM for the third straight quarter. This reflects the high-margin aftermarket flywheel: MRO utilization hit 92% across our global network, up from 85% last year, as fleets age and hours normalize. Commercial MRO grew 22% to $650 million, led by CFM56 and V2500 overhauls—our Mobile, Alabama center processed 45 shop visits using robotic stripping to cut turnaround by 30%. Defense services rose 14% on F-16 and C-130J heavy maintenance for USAF and exports, plus MQ-9 Reaper drone sustainment. APAC drove 25% growth via a Singapore MRO JV with SIA Engineering for A350/787, Middle East softened 3% on deferred spends. We're investing $250 million in digital MRO with AI predictive maintenance boosting renewals 15%. Margins hit 22.4%, our highest ever.

I'm also pleased to highlight our Aftermarket and Services segment overall, which delivered $5.2 billion, representing robust 17% year-over-year growth—the eighth straight quarter of double-digit expansion, now 42% of total revenue up from 38%. Commercial aviation aftermarket grew 22% to $3.5 billion on sustained air traffic recovery, with IATA passenger load factors at 84-86%, driving 15% more flight hours on our 25,000+ engine/component base for 737 MAX and A320neo. Shop visit rates rose with utilization over 11 hours daily for LEAP-1A/1B versus 9.5 pre-pandemic. Strong PBL demand with Southwest and Ryanair locked multi-year total care, margins up 250 bps to 52% via AeroSmart digital twins reducing unplanned removals 22% on 10 petabytes of data, partnering with Safran/MTU on LEAP. Defense services advanced 10% to $1.7 billion on F-35 ALIS/ODIN transition ramping block upgrades at Oklahoma City for 450+ aircraft, Black Hawk ops tempo up 14% on Ukraine/Indo-Pacific, and $1.2B USAF C-130J IDIQ with composite/additive repairs cutting leads 40% under AS9100D. North America 58% of growth, EMEA 25% on A320neo/Eurofighter, APAC 32% on IndiGo/AirAsia PW1100G overhauls. Inventory build ensures 98% OTD. Targeting 20%+ CAGR to 2028 with LTSAs at 65% coverage, $250M expansions including Greenville for hypersonics/eVTOL, full-year guide 16-18%.

These results tie directly to the key drivers of aftermarket performance. Fleet utilization is the primary tailwind: commercial rates rebounded to 85% of pre-pandemic, up from 72%, on 12% ASK growth per IATA, concentrated in narrowbodies where Southwest/Delta push 11+ hours/day, surging life-limited parts 22% QoQ. Defense flying hours stronger at 1.2M annualized, up 9% on NATO/Indo-Pacific ops; F-35 backlog $1.8B at 68% MC rates, allies like UK/Israel up 15% on F-16. Maintenance cycles accelerating margins: commercial C/D-checks upcycle as GTF fleet hits 40% maturity for 2.5x shop values, inductions +25% QoQ, turn times 45 days via Greenville LEAP bays. Unscheduled up 14% on APAC bird strikes/FOD, Singapore 30% share. North America 45% growth, EMEA -10% offset by pricing, APAC +28%. Digital twins/PHM via AeroEdge cut removals 17% on 4,500 engines, boosting ASPs 8%; additive for stators cuts leads to 6 weeks, +12% margins. $500M capex to 1.2M man-hours by 2026 for hypersonics/eVTOL, book-to-bill 1.3x, $15B contracts including $2.2B F-35 ALIS successor, FY25 guide 14-16%.

Before we move on, a note on our R&D investments, one of our highest priorities amid great power competition, hypersonic proliferation, and digital-physical convergence. Our $2.8 billion spend this year—up 18% YoY, 9.2% of revenues—outpaces peers. Allocation: 42% or $1.18B to air dominance like NGAD adaptive cycle engines at TRL 7, 30% thrust/25% fuel gains, 0.65 lb/lbf-hr SFC for Indo-Pacific. Hypersonics 28% or $784M on GPI Mach 7+ tests, solid-state lasers >1.5 kW/module, $450M Phase 2 vs Raytheon HBTSS, AUKUS Pillar 2. Space/C4ISR 22% or $616M on pLEO ViperSat 99.999% uptime vs jamming, quantum links 100 Gbps/1200km, 47 patents, NATO SDA 10cm res. Dual-use 8% or $224M on Orion autonomy for 4-UAV wolfpacks vs F-16s, eVTOL 500 hrs to 2026 cert. Industry R&D at 7.8%, our ROI 4.2x vs peers, NGAD pipeline +25% to $12.4B. Exports to Japan/Korea +40%, UAE directed energy. $500M AFRL CRADA metamaterials -60 dBsm RCS, 15% net-zero SAF. Risks rare earths mitigated Reno +60%. FY24 guide $3.4B +21% for CCA/counter-space, 15-20% NGAD market.

Finally, the key assumptions underpinning our full-year 2024 guidance and initial 2025 outlook. Commercial: 520-560 deliveries, 12% Q4 seq up on 737 MAX/787/A350/A321XLR ramps, supply norm at Spirit/Triumph, MRO +15% on 13 hr/day util, IATA 96% traffic, 25% APAC rev China C919/IndiGo offset Boeing pauses, 5-7% escalators. Defense 55% rev: F-35 Lot15/16 156 units to 180+ Lot17, $18B inc $12B IDIQ +8%, hypersonics $2.5B ARRW/Mayhem Glide Breaker, NGAD 1.1x book-to-bill $4B FY25, DoD $886B +2% real, intl 35% FMS Poland/GCAP €10B sensor fusion. Space $8.5B 18 Vulcan/GPS IIIF/Starshield $500M classified. Supply: 90% of 1200 suppliers norm, Ti 18mo leads, labor 4.5%, $400M YTD cost-out digital twins/GE9X AM. PT margins 85-95% yield, $300M F-35 settlements, Ukraine $61B upside. Macro 2% GDP/Fed 4.25%, Europe 20% backlog Eurofighter/FCAS, ME 15% F-15EX/THAAD, China tensions PDI boost. $2B R&D +10% peers autonomy/DE Replicator 1000+ drones, $50B services 70% stability. Stress-tested vs 10% deferral/6% inflation, upside DoD/traffic 15%+ 2025 organic.

Lisa Vargas:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, normalizing 90% of our 1,200 critical suppliers with titanium lead times down to 18 months from 36, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 LRIP and commercial deliveries. We are investing in automation and digital technologies, including digital twin factories and additive manufacturing for hot-section parts derived from GE9X tech, realizing $400 million in year-to-date cost-out while capping labor inflation at 4.5% through skills-based pay. Our MRO network utilization is at 92%, with expansions like Greenville adding capacity for LEAP swaps and hypersonic sustainment, ensuring 98% on-time delivery through strategic $800 million inventory builds.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions for queuing: please press * then 1 for questions, *2 to withdraw. Our first question comes from Josh Friedman with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Friedman:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the revenue by segment, particularly the divergence between commercial and defense growth?

Johnathan Reyes:
Certainly, Josh. As Michael detailed, commercial aerospace surged 28% to $5.2 billion on GAD-900/700 ramps and Asia-Pacific orders like the 50 narrowbody deal, despite LEAP delays, while defense grew steadily 10% to $6.1 billion on F-35 LRIP, missiles +18% post-Ukraine, and space +25%. Services +18% rounds it out, showcasing diversification. Margins expanded across, with defense book-to-bill 1.3x adding $8.2 billion awards.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the aftermarket and services revenue growth and outlook?

Michael Chen:
Emily, great question. Aftermarket hit $5.2 billion, +17% YoY, eighth double-digit quarter, now 42% of revenue. Commercial +22% on 15% flight hours/11+ util for LEAP/A320neo, PBLs with Southwest/Ryanair at 52% margins via AeroSmart AI twins -22% removals. Defense +10% on F-35/Black Hawk/C-130J, APAC +32%. Full-year 16-18%, Q4 accel F-35 lot15/LEAP 120 visits. Services flywheel with 92% util, digital PHM, targeting 20% CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Regarding the drivers of aftermarket performance, like fleet utilization and maintenance cycles—any risks there?

Dr. Elena Patel:
David, utilization drives it: commercial 85% rebound/11+ hrs narrowbodies +12% ASKs, defense 1.2M hrs +9% ops tempo F-35 68% MC. Cycles upcycle GTF 40% maturity +25% inductions/45-day turns Greenville. Unscheduled +14% APAC captured Singapore. AeroEdge -17% removals +8% ASPs, additive 12% margins. $500M capex hypersonics/eVTOL, 1.3x book-to-bill $15B backlog FY25 14-16%, contracted 75%.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question from Rahul Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Rahul Patel:
On R&D investments in next-gen platforms—how does it position you competitively?

Dr. Elena Patel:
Rahul, our $2.8B +18% YoY 9.2% rev: NGAD adaptive engines TRL7 30% thrust/25% fuel Palmdale tests, GPI hypersonics Mach7+ $450M Phase2 AUKUS, pLEO ViperSat quantum 100Gbps 47 patents NATO SDA, Orion autonomy 4-UAV Nellis vs F-16s eVTOL 500hrs. ROI 4.2x peers, NGAD $12.4B +25%, exports +40%. AFRL CRADA metamaterials, 15% net-zero. FY24 $3.4B CCA/Replicator 15-20% NGAD share.

Operator:
Next from Laura Chen with Citi.

Laura Chen:
Key assumptions for guidance—any changes with supply chain or geopolitics?

Michael Chen:
Laura, core assumptions intact: comm 520-560 deliveries +12% Q4 ramps supply norm, MRO +15% 13hr util 96% traffic 25% APAC escalators 5-7%; def F-35 156-180 units $18B hypersonics $2.5B NGAD DoD $886B intl FMS/GCAP; space $8.5B Vulcan. Supply 90% norm $400M savings, PT 85-95% Ukraine upside. Macro 2% GDP, Europe/ME contribs, $2B R&D. Stress-tested, 2025 15%+ potential.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across hypersonics, NGAD, and services stability.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
